correctness.rationale: The graph diameter is two and each nonadjacent vertex pair in fibers i-1 and i+1 has common-neighbor set exactly V_i. Hence each nonvisible set contains a unique-form forbidden fiber-plus-two-points witness. The E/P/F cyclic condition is necessary and sufficient. Classifying by numbers of full fibers gives the all-set polynomial. The augmentation tests force exactly 16 maximal cyclic words with coefficient multiplicities m^5, 5m^2, 5m and 5. All integers m>=2 are covered. Direct graph checks on 33,792 subsets for m=2,3 agree on facets, all visible sets and minimal nonfaces; finite tests are not the general proof.

originality.rationale: The proposed statement classifies every feasible and every inclusion-maximal ordinary visibility set for C5[K_m], not just their maximum sizes. Relevant first-public strong-product work (arXiv:2210.07835) proves scalar bounds and product cases but not this cyclic true-twin expansion; a 2024 diameter-two treatment (arXiv:2401.02373) covers other classes and scalar values; the full 2025 polynomial framework (doi:10.1007/s00010-025-01197-y) gives generic inclusion-exclusion but not this facet classification. Previous accessible record on clique-expanded trees is inapplicable to a cycle base. Search-negative evidence does not establish priority; unindexed equivalences are a residual risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent formula in an unindexed source or a broader theorem not identified in the searches could cover the claim; priority is provisional.

The graph is a particularly tractable diameter-two true-twin expansion; the core local rule is elementary, so mathematical value rests on complete facet classification and explicit cardinality polynomials rather than difficulty of the reduction.

value.rationale: This is a natural infinite family of strong graph products with a nontrivial five-cycle quotient. The exact ordinary-visibility face and maximal-facet polynomials, 5m^2 minimal forbidden configurations, 16 cyclic facet-state patterns with different labelled multiplicities, uniform nonpurity, and maximum-size transition at m=4 are structural complete classifications beyond a scalar graph invariant. The family supplies reusable explicit benchmark spectra for larger-cycle and unequal-fiber visibility questions; no broad algorithmic theorem is claimed.
